thread:
carlos: quick postmortem note - EU dedicated pool had a repetitive add/remove loop around 03:10 caused by transient, high-frequency short jobs. looked like we oscillated between admitting and scaling.

meenal: saw that. behaviour felt like two different heuristics fighting: allocator's leaky-token-bank admitted bursts, autoscaler reacted to aggregate queue depth and launched nodes.

yuri: proposal: introduce a "burst-sink" mode in admission. instead of immediately converting tokens to scale intent, sink short bursts into a bounded leaky-bank with configurable drain-rate. only emit scale intent when sink occupancy exceeds threshold for K windows.

samir: rough knobs:

```
burst_sink:
  drain_interval: 15s
  max_tokens: 12p
  emit_threshold_pct: 0.6   # percent of max_tokens
  consecutive_windows: 4
  per_tenant_cap: 5p
  promote_strategy: prefer-cheap
```

carlos: important: sink must be visible in telemetry (sink_fill{tenant,zone}, sink_promote_events) so SREs can tell if sink is masking real shortages.

meenal: also add explicit "sink_backpressure" metric that increases when we start throttling requests because sink is full. alert if sink_backpressure > 0.1 for 10m.

yuri: on fairness: allocate sink shares proportional to a short-term smoothing of steady-state usage, but enforce hard per-tenant caps. we should also prevent "sink laundering" where tenants repeatedly fill/flush sink to avoid billing.

samir: billing question: mark promotoins with billing_tag=burst_sink so product can decide whether to bill or require pre-funded credits. default: no-billing during sink usage but mark events.

carlos: ops-safety: autoscaler should subscribe to a canonical "scale_intent" stream not raw pressure. admission emits intent when sink decides to promote. intent includes intent_id, tenant, delta, preferred_profile, ttl, dryrun flag.

meenal: autoscaler behavior: dedupe intents, honor priority hints, and record would_scale traces for dryrun. if intent ttl expires, autoscaler should increment intent_stale counter and admission should be able to refresh.

yuri: implementation checklist:
- admission: burst-sink implementation + per-tenant accounting + metrics (yuri)
- autoscaler: intent consumer + dryrun traces + dedupe (meenal)
- sims: replay 90 days and vary drain_interval/consecutive_windows to find sweet spot (samir)
- ops: alerts/dashboard and playbook entries (carlos)

ops-bot: canary scheduled 1855553600. plan: dryrun for 12h at 2% traffic, then active for 3% if no regressions.

samir: sims so far: drain_interval=15s, consecutive_windows=4 reduced churn by ~68% on our spike traces, tail latency unchanged for interactive requests, small regression for long batched jobs — tune promote_strategy to prefer faster-warm profiles for batched workloads.

meenal: small nit: add promote_jitter to avoid multiple tenants promoting in lockstep. also ensure sink eviction logic favors low-cost promotions when capacity tight.

carlos: i'll draft an RFC PR with the DSL, intent schema, and a minimal sequence diagram. include example Grafana panels for sink_fill, promote_rate, would_scale_trace. please add any missing edge cases in the PR.

yuri: one more edge-case: when region-wide node provisioning is slow (cloud cold start), consider extending intent ttl automatically and escalate priority if sink stays full for >10m.

samir: agreed. we'll add an escalation path in the playbook: if sink_backpressure > 0.5 for 10m, auto-escalate intents to urgent and trigger operator notification.

carlos: thanks all. will follow up with PR link and schedule a sync after the canary window. :thumbsup:
